Article 63
(1) Every person/entity is prohibited from employing and involving children in the worst forms of work.
(2) The worst forms of work referred to in paragraph (1) include: a. all work in the form of slavery or similar practices; b. all work that exploits, provides or offers children for prostitution, pornography production, pornographic performances, or gambling;
c. all work that exploits, provides or involves children for the production and trade of alcoholic beverages, narcotics, psychotropic substances, and other addictive substances; and/or
d. all work that endangers the health, safety or morals of children.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Sukamara Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Sukamara. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Sukamara Regency Government. 5. Women's Empowerment is an effort to enable women to obtain access and control over economic, political and cultural resources so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 6. Women's Protection is all efforts to guarantee and protect women's rights so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination both in the form of preventive, repressive and postremedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including children who are still in the womb and not yet married. 9. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children. 10. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological to the victim. 11. Children's forum is a forum for children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 12. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government commitment and resources, community and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 13. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social. 14. Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual and social needs of citizens so that they can live decently and are able to develop themselves so that they can carry out their social functions. 15. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 18. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 19. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or outside the Country. 20. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 21. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 22. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 23. PUG focal point is an OPD operator who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 24. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive. 25. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point or from the receiving Region to the region of origin. 26. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 27. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide a sense of security to victims of violence. 28. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children so that they can grow and develop normally. 29. Spiritual guidance is an effort to provide spiritual/religious guidance. 30. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 31.

Article 78
(1) The Regent conducts supervision and evaluation of the implementation of protection of women and children periodically 1 (one) time every 3 (three) months.
(2) In conducting supervision and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regent may appoint Regional Apparatus in accordance with their duties and functions.
(3) The results of supervision and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) constitute evaluation material for policy programs on protection of women and children in the Region.

CHAPTER IV
PROTECTION OF WOMEN
Part One
General

Article 24
(1) Complaints of acts of violence against women may be made by reporters consisting of victims, family, the community and/or community organizations in the field of protection of women and children.
(2) Reports as referred to in paragraph (1) may be submitted by making complaints:
 a. directly;
 b. by telephone; and/or
 c. by letter.
(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 23 are also authorized to handle victims of acts of violence against women based on other information.
(4) Further provisions regarding procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Paragraph 2
Legal Field

Paragraph 1
General

Article 28
(1) The Regional Government may provide safe houses for women victims of acts of violence.
(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in Article 26 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of acts of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
(4) The criteria for women victims of acts of violence who require safe houses include:
   a. their life is threatened;
   b. receiving rejection from family or community;
   c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
   d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
(5) The implementation of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
   a. social workers/volunteers;
   b. security officers; and/or
   c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the implementation of safe house services are regulated in Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER X
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 76
(1) Guidance on women's empowerment and child protection is carried out by the Regional Government.
(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out in the form of:
a. providing training for government officials and law enforcement regarding prevention;
b. providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, customary leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children;
c. providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units and general hospitals;
d. providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and children victims of violence; and
e. conducting professional improvement for officers, managers of violence case data against women and children at community health centers, integrated service units and general hospitals.
(3) The Regent has the authority to conduct guidance in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection.

Part Two
Prevention of Acts of Violence Against Women

CHAPTER II
RIGHTS OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
Article 3
Every woman and child has basic rights as a human being that must be protected, promoted, upheld and fulfilled in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 20
Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear.
Paragraph (2)
Point a What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring problems experienced by victims and be able to empower victims.
Point b Sufficiently clear.
Point c What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing beliefs, values, and social status.
Point d What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service provision process must be kept confidential and known only to people who are relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to victims.
Point e What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that officers providing services must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems.
Point f What is meant by respecting individual differences (individual differences) is that each individual must be viewed as unique; each person has a different background, life experience, and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism), so that one victim must not be compared with another victim in any matter.
Point g What is meant by non-judgmental is that officers providing services must ensure that whatever the victim's condition, they will not be assessed or judged.
Point h What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent.
Point i What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using language that is appropriate and understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational, and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers; it must be ensured that victims are served in language understood by the victim. Lately, there are increasingly more disabled/difable/disable women who become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind, or those experiencing mental retardation. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided, for example from special education school teachers.
Point j What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties; however, with proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral cover letter, and efforts must be made so that the victim is not asked repeatedly about the same things related to identity or the case narrative.
Point k What is meant by "empat", namely the ability to place oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood, and can openly tell their problems.
Point l What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survival, development, protection, freedom from all forms of discrimination, and participation, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women.

Paragraph 3
Social Sector

Article 54
(1) Regional Governments are obligated to provide comprehensive health services for children, so that every child obtains optimal health status from the time they are in the womb.
(2) Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services and care; and
b. exemption from cost burden for malnourished children, children with disabilities, children with special needs, children infected with HIV/AIDS, child laborers, child victims of narcotics abuse, alcohol, psychotropic substances, and other addictive substances, children who are victims of violence and child victims of human trafficking.
(3) Regional Governments, communities, families and parents are obligated to make efforts so that children who are born are protected from diseases that threaten survival and/or cause disability.

HEAD OF LEGAL DIVISION,
DEWA PUTU OKA, S.H. NIP. 19750815 200212 1 004
ELUCIDATION
ON
REGIONAL REGULATION OF SUKAMARA REGENCY
NUMBER 9 OF 2022
CONCERNING
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION
1. GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution as a Constitutional foundation has explicitly regulated the importance of protection of Human Rights, including the rights of women and children. In addition to the guarantee from the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, the guarantee that every person must have equal dignity and degree has also been recognized internationally. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights or UDHR of 1948 which underlies Human Rights in general has guaranteed that all people are born with freedom, having equal dignity and rights without exception.

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the Regional Government to regulate and manage regional government affairs aimed at realizing community welfare through improved services, protection and empowerment of the community. As a component of society that plays an important role in realizing a quality generation and as successors to the nation's struggle, women and children must receive guarantees for the fulfillment of children's rights.

To ensure the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in accordance with human dignity and in order to carry out mandatory affairs, regional governments need to provide legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection through the formulation of a policy. The formulation of such policy is a form of support and concrete effort from various other parties in ensuring the fulfillment of the rights of women and children.

The Implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is carried out based on the principles of:
a. non-discrimination;
b. the best interests of women and children;
c. the right to life, survival and development;
d. respect for children and legal certainty; and
e. local wisdom and justice and gender equality.

The formulation of the Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection aims to:
a. provide guidance in planning and implementing Women's Empowerment and Child Protection policies;
b. increase efforts for Women's Empowerment and fulfillment of children's rights in order to realize improved quality of life for women and children in the Region;
c. increase protection efforts for women and children from actions and policies that violate the rights of women and children;
d. increase the value of local wisdom and the role of customs in Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, and
e. increase the role of Regional Government and other community institutions in efforts for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation on Women and Child Protection regulates:
a. Improvement of women's quality of life which contains government responsibilities, implementation of PUG, Efforts to increase the role, quality and capacity of women in the political, legal, social and economic fields;
b. Protection of women which contains regional government responsibilities in women's protection, prevention of violence against women, protection for women victims of violence, as well as complaint handling,
c. Article 2
The Women's Empowerment and Child Protection System aims to:
a. improve the quality of life of women, children, and the quality of families;
b. increase the institutional capacity of women's empowerment and child protection in Sukamara Regency, including the development of gender and child data systems; and
c. provide protection of women's rights and fulfillment of children's rights including special protection for children from various forms of violence and other discriminatory treatment.

Article 20
Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear.
Paragraph (2)
Point a What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring problems experienced by victims and be able to empower victims.
Point b Sufficiently clear.
Point c What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing beliefs, values, and social status.
Point d What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service provision process must be kept confidential and known only to people who are relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to victims.
Point e What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that officers providing services must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems.
Point f What is meant by respecting individual differences (individual differences) is that each individual must be viewed as unique; each person has a different background, life experience, and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism), so that one victim must not be compared with another victim in any matter.
Point g What is meant by non-judgmental is that officers providing services must ensure that whatever the victim's condition, they will not be assessed or judged.
Point h What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent.
Point i What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using language that is appropriate and understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational, and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers; it must be ensured that victims are served in language understood by the victim. Lately, there are increasingly more disabled/difable/disable women who become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind, or those experiencing mental retardation. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided, for example from special education school teachers.
Point j What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties; however, with proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral cover letter, and efforts must be made so that the victim is not asked repeatedly about the same things related to identity or the case narrative.
Point k What is meant by "empat", namely the ability to place oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood, and can openly tell their problems.
Point l What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survival, development, protection, freedom from all forms of discrimination, and participation, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women.

(1) Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 22 letter c, is intended to restore and develop the capabilities of women victims of violence who experience social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions in society properly.

a. counseling;
b. provision of safe houses; and
c. spiritual guidance.
(3) The implementation of services as referred to in paragraph (2) is carried out by:
a. PD that administers governmental affairs in the social sector;
b. PD that administers governmental affairs in the sector of women and child empowerment, and may cooperate with an integrated service center (women crisis center) or existing community organizations in the social sector; or
c. religious institutions and/or organizations.

Article 51
(1) Every organizer of an educational unit is obligated to provide opportunities for children to obtain services without discrimination.
(2) Every organizer of an educational unit is prohibited from expelling children from educational institutions unless there is a guarantee for the continuity of the child's education.

Article 53

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear.
Paragraph (2)

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Sukamara Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Sukamara. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Sukamara Regency Government. 5. Women's Empowerment is an effort to enable women to obtain access and control over economic, political and cultural resources so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 6. Women's Protection is all efforts to guarantee and protect women's rights so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination both in the form of preventive, repressive and postremedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old, including children who are still in the womb and not yet married. 9. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children. 10. Violence is any act that results in or can result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological to the victim. 11. Children's forum is a forum for children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 12. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government commitment and resources, community and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 13. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social. 14. Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual and social needs of citizens so that they can live decently and are able to develop themselves so that they can carry out their social functions. 15. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 18. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 19. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or outside the Country. 20. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 21. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 22. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 23. PUG focal point is an OPD operator who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 24. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive. 25. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point or from the receiving Region to the region of origin. 26. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 27. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide a sense of security to victims of violence. 28. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children so that they can grow and develop normally. 29. Spiritual guidance is an effort to provide spiritual/religious guidance. 30. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 31.

CHAPTER X
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 76
(1) Guidance on women's empowerment and child protection is carried out by the Regional Government.
(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out in the form of:
a. providing training for government officials and law enforcement regarding prevention;
b. providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, customary leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children;
c. providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units and general hospitals;
d. providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and children victims of violence; and

Children in conflict with the law, children experiencing pregnancy outside of marriage and/or an unwanted pregnancy, and children who are victims of HIV/AIDS infection are protected in their right to obtain education.

(1) Regional Governments are obligated to provide comprehensive health services for children, so that every child obtains optimal health status from the time they are in the womb.
(2) Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services and care; and

Social Sector

CONCERNING

1. GENERAL
The 1945 Constitution as a Constitutional foundation has explicitly regulated the importance of protection of Human Rights, including the rights of women and children. In addition to the guarantee from the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, the guarantee that every person must have equal dignity and degree has also been recognized internationally. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights or UDHR of 1948 which underlies Human Rights in general has guaranteed that all people are born with freedom, having equal dignity and rights without exception.

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates the Regional Government to regulate and manage regional government affairs aimed at realizing community welfare through improved services, protection and empowerment of the community. As a component of society that plays an important role in realizing a quality generation and as successors to the nation's struggle, women and children must receive guarantees for the fulfillment of children's rights.

To ensure the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in accordance with human dignity and in order to carry out mandatory affairs, regional governments need to provide legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection through the formulation of a policy. The formulation of such policy is a form of support and concrete effort from various other parties in ensuring the fulfillment of the rights of women and children.

The Implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is carried out based on the principles of:
a. non-discrimination;
b. the best interests of women and children;
c. the right to life, survival and development;
d. respect for children and legal certainty; and
e. local wisdom and justice and gender equality.

The formulation of the Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection aims to:
a. provide guidance in planning and implementing Women's Empowerment and Child Protection policies;
b. increase efforts for Women's Empowerment and fulfillment of children's rights in order to realize improved quality of life for women and children in the Region;
c. increase protection efforts for women and children from actions and policies that violate the rights of women and children;
d. increase the value of local wisdom and the role of customs in Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, and
e. increase the role of Regional Government and other community institutions in efforts for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

This Regional Regulation on Women and Child Protection regulates:
a. Improvement of women's quality of life which contains government responsibilities, implementation of PUG, Efforts to increase the role, quality and capacity of women in the political, legal, social and economic fields;
b. Protection of women which contains regional government responsibilities in women's protection, prevention of violence against women, protection for women victims of violence, as well as complaint handling,
c. Child Protection which contains the responsibilities of regional government, parents/families and the community in protecting children as well as efforts made by regional governments in implementing child protection. In addition, the need to establish a children's forum and Child-Friendly Regency as a form of appreciation in realizing protection and fulfillment of children's rights.

(1) Complaints of acts of violence against women may be made by reporters consisting of victims, family, the community and/or community organizations in the field of protection of women and children.
(2) Reports as referred to in paragraph (1) may be submitted by making complaints:

 b. by telephone; and/or
 c. by letter.
(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 23 are also authorized to handle victims of acts of violence against women based on other information.
(4) Further provisions regarding procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be regulated in a Regent Regulation.

5.4.rationale: The original Indonesian text engages education institutions directly. Pasal 51 regulates “penyelenggara satuan pendidikan” (education unit organizers): they must provide non-discriminatory access (ayat (1)), are prohibited from expelling children without ensuring continuity (ayat (2)), and if a child victim of violence drops out, the education organizer must coordinate with relevant agencies (ayat (3)). Pasal 70 huruf c also includes “mengembangkan model sekolah ramah anak” (develop child-friendly school models). These show explicit engagement of the education sector. The retrieved passages include these points and the judge’s “Yes” aligns with the text, so the golden label “No” appears wrong.

6.4.evaluator_rationale: None of the cited sentences mention elderly women or provide measures specifically targeted to older/elderly women; the provisions are general to women or to other groups (e.g., workers, victims of violence).

Point a What is meant by gender responsive is that all service officers must be gender sensitive when exploring problems experienced by victims and be able to empower victims.
Point b Sufficiently clear.
Point c What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim, the provision of services for victims must be carried out with respect for the victim without distinguishing beliefs, values, and social status.
Point d What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the victim's privacy. Every piece of information revealed in the service provision process must be kept confidential and known only to people who are relevant in providing services. Officers must convey this principle to victims.
Point e What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that officers providing services must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems.
Point f What is meant by respecting individual differences (individual differences) is that each individual must be viewed as unique; each person has a different background, life experience, and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism), so that one victim must not be compared with another victim in any matter.
Point g What is meant by non-judgmental is that officers providing services must ensure that whatever the victim's condition, they will not be assessed or judged.
Point h What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that service provision must be carried out with the victim's consent.
Point i What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using language that is appropriate and understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational, and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the officers; it must be ensured that victims are served in language understood by the victim. Lately, there are increasingly more disabled/difable/disable women who become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind, or those experiencing mental retardation. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided, for example from special education school teachers.
Point j What is meant by fast and simple is that service provision must be given immediately without delay involving various parties; however, with proactive service officers, victims must be guaranteed to go through everything with a simple process. If the victim comes on referral from another service provider, the receiving officer must first read the referral cover letter, and efforts must be made so that the victim is not asked repeatedly about the same things related to identity or the case narrative.
Point k What is meant by "empat", namely the ability to place oneself in the position of others (in this case the victim). Thus the victim feels accepted, understood, and can openly tell their problems.
Point l What is meant by fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survival, development, protection, freedom from all forms of discrimination, and participation, as regulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women.

Article 25
(1) Health Rehabilitation as referred to in Article 22 letter b, constitutes efforts that include aspects of:
a. promotive;
b. preventive;
c. curative; and
d. rehabilitative.
(2) Health rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted comprehensively, accessible 24 (twenty-four) hours at RSUD and conducted in accordance with health service standards.
(3) Women victims of acts of violence have the right to health services free of charge for both medical costs, medicolegal and visum.
(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures for implementation of Health Rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be regulated in the Regent Regulation.

Article 33
(1) Social reintegration as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (2) is carried out in the context of reuniting women victims of acts of violence with substitute family parties, or communities that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
(2) Social reintegration is aimed so that:
a. women victims of acts of violence can resume their social life; and
b. women victims of acts of violence can have a decent life.
(3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after victims receive social rehabilitation services.

6.4.rationale: The original Indonesian text addresses elderly (lansia) within family quality improvement measures: Pasal 39 huruf c states “peningkatan kualitas hidup lanjut usia melalui program pembinaan lansia, bina keluarga lansia, pembinaan dan bimbingan lansia” (improving quality of life of the elderly through elderly guidance programs, elderly-family development, etc.). While this is not phrased as “elderly women” specifically, it is the only clear elderly-targeted content in the regulation and could support a “Yes” depending on the indicator definition used by the human coder. None of the retrieved candidate passages for 6.4 included Pasal 39 (or any mention of “lanjut usia/lansia”), so the judge had no evidence to answer Yes and predicted No. This points to retrieval failure for the elderly-related provision.
